claim: Rewarding only difference from past behaviour (novelty plus archive) solved a deceptive maze in 39/40 runs; goal-fitness NEAT 3/40, random 4/40 (hard map); on the medium map novelty took 18,274 evals vs 56,334.
agent_test: Same-token comparison: an agent told to pursue the goal vs one scored on distance from its own earlier attempts, on deceptive puzzles.

claim: Novelty search is not a universal win: in the unenclosed maze it solved 5/100 vs fitness 2/100 (not significant); it needs a behaviour space where being new correlates with progress.
agent_test: Include tasks where novelty is uncorrelated with progress and check the agent does not drift.

claim: Novelty search is sensitive to the behaviour characterisation: irrelevant behaviour dimensions (3-4 extra points) made 21-29 of 70 runs fail, wrong aliasing solved only 6/70, and coarse cells larger than mutation range collapsed performance.
schema_part: O/S (what counts as a different attempt)
agent_test: Vary the descriptor of 'different answer' (embedding, approach label, final answer) and measure the effect on solve rate.
audit_note: Lehman and Stanley found coarse behaviour grids barely hurt (except 4x4), which is a different setting from Kistemaker's supercell result; claim numbers (21/70, 29/70, 6/70, cell size vs mutation range) match Kistemaker.

claim: Hybrids of novelty and objective (50/50 blend, multi-objective NSGA) beat pure novelty or pure fitness on success ratio in mazes (p<0.01); a random archive and k in 15-100 worked best.
agent_test: Mix a goal-score term with a difference term at equal tokens; compare against both pure arms.

claim: Archive size matters little in the maze: an archive capped at population size solved 40/40, no different from unbounded.
agent_test: Cap the list of past attempts shown to the agent and check whether it hurts.

claim: Quality-diversity (MAP-Elites) gives better coverage and reliability than optimisation controls, but not a better single best solution (p>0.05 in soft robots).
agent_test: Measure coverage of distinct solution types and best answer separately; expect coverage gains, not best-answer gains.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: In deep RL, adding novelty to evolution strategies escapes a deceptive trap that plain ES never leaves (10 of 10 runs stuck), and NSRA-ES (adaptive blend) beats NS-ES and NSR-ES (p<0.01).
agent_test: Adaptive weight on novelty: raise it when progress stalls, lower it when progress arrives.

claim: Bonus-based exploration is weaker than hoped in standard benchmarks: with Rainbow, pseudo-count was worse on almost all training games and RND/ICM only matched epsilon-greedy.
agent_test: Warning: do not assume a novelty bonus helps without a control arm.

claim: Go-Explore (archive, return, then explore) reached far beyond intrinsic-motivation agents on Montezuma and Pitfall (arXiv: mean 43,763 without domain knowledge, 666,474 with it; Nature version robustified mean 1.73 million).
schema_part: memory/O (archive of promising states, return to them)
agent_test: Let the agent keep an archive of partial solutions and restart from them versus from scratch.

claim: Learned novelty in representation space beat random-reward exploration in Acrobot (576 vs 1713 steps) and a multi-step maze (525 vs 1863), but was not significantly different from RND on Acrobot (592.5, p=0.85). Only 5 trials.
agent_test: Treat as weak: small n, one author group.

claim: Open-ended systems with a growing archive keep improving where fixed or no-archive controls plateau: POET/Enhanced POET, OMNI-EPIC, Darwin Godel Machine (SWE-bench 20.0% to 50.0%, Polyglot 14.2% to 30.7%; ablation without open-ended archive progressed much less).
agent_test: Ablate the archive of past attempts in a long multi-round run at equal tokens.
audit_note: Enhanced POET plateau comparison is against original POET (ANNECS plateau after ~20,000 iterations), not a no-archive control; HGM re-run shows DGM improves but is beaten by HGM.

claim: An LLM model of interestingness focuses exploration: OMNI beat uniform and learning-progress task choice (Crafter 82 tasks learned, 14 interesting, success 0.78 on interesting tasks vs LP 55/9/0.52; AI2-THOR 13 vs 2 tasks at >=0.6).
agent_test: Use the model itself to judge which candidate directions are interesting and learnable, not just new.

claim: The judges used in LLM open-endedness systems are only moderately reliable: OMNI-EPIC success detector 72.7% agreement with 50 humans; ACD 92.2% of tasks valid; QDAIF human-AI agreement 0.833 vs human-human 0.800. Self-judging adds bias: GPT-4 is 73.5% accurate at recognising its own summaries and self-preference strength is linearly correlated with self-recognition; pairwise LLM judging reaches 61-71% on paper acceptance; judge-human agreement is lowest on similar-quality items.
agent_test: Measure the agent's self-judged novelty against an external judge; report agreement.
audit_note: Panickssery et al. report GPT-4 is 73.5% accurate at distinguishing its own summaries from other LLMs' and humans' (self-recognition), not that it picks its own text 73.5% of the time; the other numbers (72.7%, 92.2%, 0.833 vs 0.800, 61.1-71.4%) match.
claim_before_audit: The judges used in LLM open-endedness systems are only moderately reliable: OMNI-EPIC success detector 72.7% agreement with 50 humans; ACD 92.2% of tasks valid; QDAIF human-AI agreement 0.833 vs human-human 0.800. Self-judging adds bias: GPT-4 picks its own text 73.5% of the time and self-preference tracks self-recognition; pairwise LLM judging reaches 61-71% on paper acceptance; judge-human agreement is lowest on similar-quality items.

claim: QDAIF raises automatic quality-diversity over baselines in all its domains, but the human-rated margin is tiny: human QD 0.772 vs Fixed-Few-Shot 0.767, and Fixed-Few-Shot had higher human quality (4.133 vs 3.900).
agent_test: Compare diversity-guided search against plain few-shot at equal tokens; do not expect large human-rated gains.

claim: Voyager's automatic curriculum plus skill library drove open-ended Minecraft progress: 63 unique items, 3.3x baselines; random curriculum cut items by 93%; without the skill library no diamond (0/3 vs 1/3). Only 3 trials.
agent_test: Ablate a skill/insight library and a curriculum in a multi-round task.

claim: Frontier chat LLMs give little variety: fewer than 3 distinct answers in 10 samples at temperature 1 (Claude-3.5 Sonnet 1.76, gpt-4o 2.88); small models were most diverse (Gemma-2-2B 5.66). In-context regeneration helps. Temperature is not a fix: in Llama 2-Chat 70B stories it was only weakly correlated with novelty and moderately with incoherence; even min-p at temperature 2.0 left same-prompt similarity above 0.8 (Artificial Hivemind).
agent_test: Run NoveltyBench-style distinct counts with and without a forced 'differ from previous answers' step at equal tokens.

claim: LLM-generated research ideas were rated more novel than human ideas (5.64 vs 4.84, p<0.01, 49 ideas per condition), but generation saturates: about 200 non-duplicates out of 4000 per topic.
agent_test: Track duplicate rate across rounds; stop adding rounds when the new share falls.

claim: Rainbow Teaming's archive of diverse prompts reached about 92-98% attack success after 2000 iterations; fine-tuning on it cut success to under 1%; about 50% of prompts transfer to other models.
agent_test: Use a feature-grid archive for adversarial self-testing at fixed token budget.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLM-driven mutation (diff models) is more robust than random code mutation: GP success fell to zero at 5 bugs while diff mutation degraded only at the 5th bug type; fine-tuning on accepted diffs raised niche coverage.
agent_test: Compare LLM proposals as the variation operator against random edits.

claim: Partly tested now: forcing different ideas (PlanSearch) raised LLM code correctness at equal attempts (LiveCodeBench pass@200 60.6 to 73.0 GPT-4o, 55.6 to 77.0 Claude 3.5 Sonnet), and an answer-novelty bonus in RL raised math pass@k slightly. Still untested: a prompt-time difference-from-earlier-attempts operator at equal TOKENS on general reasoning, and on non-code tasks; gains vanish for a model that already searches (o1-mini).
agent_test: Direct test: scaffold with and without a difference-from-prior-attempts operator on a benchmark with deceptive first answers.

claim: At equal number of attempts, searching over different natural-language plans beat repeated sampling on code: LiveCodeBench pass@200 GPT-4o-mini 53.3 to 64.9, GPT-4o 60.6 to 73.0, DeepSeek-Coder-V2 53.2 to 70.3, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 55.6 to 77.0. Pass@1 often drops. Gain nearly vanishes for o1-mini (90.8 to 91.3). Compute-normalised results not read.
agent_test: A/B the approach-forcing operator against plain best-of-k at equal tokens, report pass@1 and pass@k separately.

claim: Descriptor choice: the diversity that predicts search gain is at idea level, scored by an LLM on pairs; token entropy is insufficient. Answer-class novelty works in math RL (few outcome classes). Embedding similarity stays above 0.8 even at temperature 2.0, so embeddings plus sampling noise are a weak descriptor.
agent_test: Compare approach-label, final-answer class and embedding descriptors on the same task set.

claim: Adding a novelty bonus to goal-only LLM RL can help: an answer-novelty bonus needed a baseline to improve test pass@k (naive UCB did not), and rewarding rare-but-correct proofs raised pass@N where goal-only GRPO sharpened and lost to base sampling at large N; goal-only RL narrows coverage (base beats RL at large k, e.g. 128-256). Novelty-only LLM RL and adaptive-weight rules (as in NSRA-ES) were not tested in these sources.
agent_test: Keep a goal term in every score; test fixed 50/50 against adaptive weight raised on stall.
audit_note: The sources compare goal-only RL with goal plus novelty/rarity bonuses (Song et al.: bonus needs a baseline, naive UCB did not help test performance; He et al.: GRPO sharpens and underperforms base sampling at large N; Yue et al.: base beats RL at large k), but none tests novelty-only RL, so 'beats either alone' is wider than the evidence.
claim_before_audit: Blending goal and novelty beats either alone in LLM RL: answer-novelty bonus needs a baseline to generalise (naive UCB did not), and rewarding rare-and-correct solutions raised pass@N where goal-only GRPO sharpened and lost to base sampling at large N. Goal-only RL narrows coverage (base beats RL at k=128-256). No adaptive-weight rule (as in NSRA-ES) was tested for LLMs.

claim: Coverage grows log-linearly with samples (SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples) but unverified selection plateaus (MATH: 82.9% to 98.44% coverage vs 40.50% to 41.41% by vote or reward model). Archive size beyond several hundred is wasted without a verifier. Shown-in-context versus silent filtering is untested.
agent_test: Cap archive at tens of items in context; test filtering versus showing.

claim: Returning to stored partial solutions beat independent restarts on Game of 24 (ToT b=5 74% vs CoT best of 100 49%) but cost more ($0.74 vs $0.47 per case) and the paper has no equal-token curve; return was by LLM value check, not novelty.
agent_test: Compare restart versus resume-from-best-partial at equal tokens.

claim: Novelty failure modes: surprise-driven agents slow down sharply when a random-noise source is present (noisy TV, qualitative). Judged novelty of ideas fell by 1.05 points on a 1-10 scale after execution while human ideas did not (43 projects), so pre-execution novelty overstates value.
agent_test: Add a noise-only distractor to a test task and check the operator ignores it; score difference after outcome.

claim: Independent replication is thin: only HGM (a rival lab) re-ran DGM as a baseline with different backbones (DGM reached 53.3 on SWE-Verified-60 and 27.1 on Polyglot there; the original paper reports 50.0 and 30.7 on other setups, so direction reproduced, numbers not comparable). No outside replication of Voyager or OMNI was found in this search.
agent_test: Treat headline numbers of Voyager, OMNI, DGM as lab-reported.
